newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia aims to boost beef share in S.Korea.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia aims to boost beef share in S.Korea.

text.p: Australian meat exports are expected to gain market share in South Korea with the liberalisation of that country's market, the Australian Meat and Livestock Corp (AMLC) said on Tuesday.
Each step toward liberalisation of the South Korean market offered increased opportunities for Australia's beef industry, AMLC beef programme manager Allister Lugsdin said in a statement.
Under the Uruguay Round of trade liberalisation, the Korean quota on beef imports is scheduled to increase each year until liberalisation of the market in 2001, he said.

Not only is the volume of imports rising, the percentage of the quota allocated to private sector groups under the Simultaneous Buy Sell (SBS) system is also increasing. This offers opportunities for marketing a broader range of product, he said.
The Korean beef import quota is divided between the government buying authority, Livestock Products Marketing Organisation (LPMO), and the private sector under the SBS quota.
Between now and 2001, the LPMO share of the quota will gradually reduce to 30 percent and the SBS share will rise to 70 percent, he said.
South Korea's private sector is presently importing 40 percent of the country's intake against 60 percent by the LPMO.
"In 1997, for the first time, the SBS share will be equal to that of the LPMO," Lugsdin said.
"With the opportunity to import more product the buying groups allowed to purchase under this system are likely to expand their product range," he said.

"(Australia's) Korean marketing programme is designed to capitalise on this by working closely with the trade in Korea to make them aware of the range and quality of beef products Australia has to offer."
Australia's share of the South Korean beef import market in the 1996 quota year was 31 percent, steady with the previous year, against nearly 52 percent held by the U.S.

In total beef exports projected by the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics at A$2.2 billion for 1996/97 ending June 30, Australia is projected to export 60,000 tonnes to South Kore against 330,000 tonnes to Japan and 170,000 tonnes to the U.S.
